title: wsutil: Add an application flavor API
description:
Remove the configuration namespace routines and macros in
filesystem.[ch] with an application flavor API defined and implemented
in application_flavor.[ch].

This would fix #20209, I think, by defaulting to `APPLICATION_FLAVOR_WIRESHARK` rather than an "uninitialized" value as it does currently, which has the effect of sometimes giving the same paths as Stratoshark, sometimes giving the Wireshark paths, and sometimes looking in the home directory.
It defaults to `APPLICATION_FLAVOR_WIRESHARK` now.

Took me a bit to figure this out (!18141) when it defaulted to Wireshark.  
(If we were at Sharkfest with a whiteboard and cup of coffee I would be in full "Pepe Silvia" mode)

Done, although we really just want the executable name here. Maybe it would make sense to call `g_set_prgname` in `configuration_init_posix` and `configuration_init_w32` so that we can call `g_get_prgname` elsewhere?
Yes, we should probably call `g_set_prgname()`, or some routine that calls it, early in `main()` for all *Shark programs.  `ws_log_init()` calls it, but that's not an obvious side effect.
OK, I switched it to `g_get_prgname`.

Now "flavor" not "namespace"?
We don't need the dumpcap-specific part.

> Now "flavor" not "namespace"?

Yes, as per the title of the merge request.

Think of "Wireshark" as a family of software suites, a packet analyzer suite named Wireshark and a log analyzer suite named Stratoshark.  At some point there may be a file analyzer suite named Fileshark.

This specifies the family. Various parts of the code that are shared between suites may do different things, including but not limited to using different file system pathnames depending on the suite to which the program calling that code belongs.

+/** @file
+ * Application flavor definitions
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <wireshark.h>
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+/*
+ * Application flavor. Used to construct configuration
+ * paths and environment variables.
+ */
+enum application_flavor_e {
+    APPLICATION_FLAVOR_WIRESHARK,
+    APPLICATION_FLAVOR_STRATOSHARK,
+};
+
+/**
+ * Initialize our application flavor.
+ *
+ * Set our application flavor, which determines the top-level
+ * configuration directory name and environment variable prefixes.
+ * Default is APPLICATION_FLAVOR_WIRESHARK.
+ *
+ * @param flavor Application flavor.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC void set_application_flavor(enum application_flavor_e flavor);
+
+/**
+ * Get our application flavor.
+ * @return The flavor.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC enum application_flavor_e get_application_flavor(void);
+
+/**
+ * Get the proper (capitalized) application name, suitable for user
+ * presentation.
+ *
+ * @return The application name. Must not be freed.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC const char *application_flavor_name_proper(void);
+
+/**
+ * Get the lower-case application name.
+ *
+ * @return The application name. Must not be freed.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC const char *application_flavor_name_lower(void);
+
+/**
+ * Convenience routine for checking the application flavor.
+ * @return true if the application flavor is APPLICATION_FLAVOR_WIRESHARK.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC bool application_flavor_is_wireshark(void);
+
+/**
+ * Convenience routine for checking the application flavor.
+ * @return true if the application flavor is APPLICATION_FLAVOR_STRATOSHARK.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC bool application_flavor_is_stratoshark(void);
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
